title: Over-collection of PII during registration
description: Parent user shares excessive personally identifiable information including government ID, email, name, and password during registration, creating identification risks and potential for data misuse.

title: Linkability of registration data in transit
description: Registration data transmitted between parent user and authentication service could be intercepted and linked to identify the user across systems or correlate with other data sources.

title: Interception of six-digit verification code
description: The six-digit verification code transmitted during registration could be intercepted by attackers, enabling unauthorized account creation or takeover.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of government ID data
description: Authentication service receives and stores sensitive government ID information, creating risk of unauthorized access, data breaches, or improper sharing with third parties.

title: Persistent identification through stored registration data
description: Authentication service stores parent registration data (name, email, government ID) enabling persistent identification of the user across sessions and potential profiling.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Parent Account Data
description: The MongoDB users collection stores sensitive parent account information. If access controls are inadequate, unauthorized parties could access this data, leading to privacy violations.

title: Data Integrity Compromise of Stored Parent Account Data
description: The stored parent account data could be tampered with or corrupted during storage, potentially leading to incorrect authentication or account management.

title: Identification Through Parent Account Data Sharing
description: The Authentication Service shares parent account information, which could be used to identify individuals and link them to their accounts.

title: User data identifiable in transit
description: User data transmitted in JWT format may contain personally identifiable information that could be extracted or linked to the parent user during transmission.

title: JWT token interception during transmission
description: JWT tokens containing user authentication data may be intercepted by unauthorized parties during data flow transmission if not properly encrypted or secured.

title: Parent user misuse of authentication data
description: The parent user (destination) may misuse the received JWT and user data for unauthorized access or activities beyond intended scope.

title: Linkability of Child to Parent Identity
description: The child user sharing parent email and password credentials creates a link between the child's account activities and the parent's identity, potentially exposing the parent's personal information through the child's usage patterns.

title: Credential Interception During Transmission
description: Parent email and password credentials transmitted in the data flow could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, enabling identification of the parent and potential unauthorized access to their account.

title: Credential Usurpation in Transit
description: Intercepted credentials during transmission could be used by malicious actors to usurp the parent's identity and gain unauthorized access to their account or associated services.

title: Improper Credential Storage and Access
description: The authentication service may store or access parent credentials inappropriately, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive authentication information and potential identity theft.

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: The authentication service may not comply with applicable privacy regulations regarding the collection, storage, and processing of parent credentials, resulting in regulatory violations and potential legal consequences.

title: Identification through intercepted JWT and profile data
description: JWT tokens and child profile data transmitted in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, enabling identification of the child user through the contained personal information.

title: Excessive data sharing by Authentication Service
description: The Authentication Service may share more child profile data than necessary for the authentication purpose, violating data minimization principles.

title: Unauthorized use of child data by recipient
description: The Child User may misuse the received JWT and profile data for unauthorized purposes, potentially sharing it with third parties or using it beyond the intended scope.

title: Unauthorized identification of child through data in transit
description: Sensitive child profile data (name, DOB, government ID) transmitted in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, enabling identification of the child through the combination of personally identifiable information.

title: Parent's act of sharing child data creates linkability risk
description: Parent sharing child's government ID and personal information creates opportunities for linking this data with other datasets, potentially enabling profiling or tracking of the child across systems.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child profile data
description: Child profile management system may store sensitive data without adequate access controls, leading to potential unauthorized disclosure of the child's personally identifiable information to unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Child Profiles
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB collection could be accessed by unauthorized parties if access controls are insufficient, leading to privacy violations of children and their guardians.

title: Data Integrity Compromise
description: Child profile data could be tampered with or corrupted during storage, leading to inaccurate records that could affect child welfare decisions or parental access.

title: Data Unavailability
description: Child profile data could become unavailable due to system failures, ransomware attacks, or service disruptions, preventing authorized access when needed.

title: GDPR Compliance Violation
description: Storing children's personal data may violate GDPR requirements for special category data, requiring additional protections and consent mechanisms that may not be in place.

title: Identification via Video Metadata
description: Video metadata (timestamps, location data, device information) could be used to identify the child user or their family, potentially revealing sensitive personal information about their location, routines, or activities.

title: Video Content Leakage in Transit
description: Video content transmitted between the child user and the Video Management Service could be intercepted or leaked, exposing the child's activities, surroundings, or personal information to unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized Access to Video Content
description: Video content and associated metadata could be accessed by unauthorized third parties during transmission, potentially violating the child's privacy and exposing sensitive information.

title: Child User Self-Identification Risk
description: The child user may inadvertently share identifying information through video content, comments, or search queries, potentially revealing their identity, location, or personal circumstances.

title: Inappropriate Data Processing by Service
description: The Video Management Service may process or store video content in ways that violate child privacy regulations, such as retaining data longer than necessary or using it for purposes beyond the stated service.

title: Lack of Action Non-Repudiation
description: Child user actions (likes, comments, video requests) may not be properly logged or authenticated, making it difficult to verify or defend against false claims about what the child did or said.

title: Identification through video metadata in transit
description: Video metadata (e.g., timestamps, locations, participants) transmitted between Video Management Service and MongoDB could be intercepted and used to identify individuals or link them to specific events.

title: Linkability of video data across sessions
description: Video metadata and files in transit could be correlated across different sessions or users, enabling tracking of individuals or linking disparate data points.

title: Unauthorized access to stored video data
description: MongoDB videos collection may have insufficient access controls, allowing unauthorized parties to access, view, or download stored video files and metadata.

title: Data misuse through improper retention
description: Video data stored in MongoDB may be retained longer than necessary or accessed for purposes beyond the original collection intent, leading to privacy violations.

title: Inappropriate data sharing by Video Management Service
description: The Video Management Service may share video metadata and files with MongoDB without proper authorization or consent from data subjects.

title: Unauthorized Access to Child Search and Watch History
description: Child search and watch history stored in MongoDB may be accessed by unauthorized parties due to insufficient access controls and authentication mechanisms at the destination data store.

title: Identification Through Search and Watch History
description: Search and watch history data can be used to identify children's interests, preferences, and potentially link them to specific profiles or activities, revealing sensitive information about the child.

title: Excessive Retention of Children's Search and Watch History
description: Child search and watch history may be retained longer than necessary, violating data minimization principles and children's privacy rights, especially given the sensitive nature of children's data.

title: Insecure Storage of Sensitive Child Data
description: MongoDB collection may not be properly secured with encryption, access controls, or other security measures, leading to potential data breaches and unauthorized access to sensitive child information.

title: Inappropriate Data Collection Without Consent
description: The Child Profile Management process may be collecting and storing child search and watch history without proper parental consent or without ensuring the child understands what data is being collected.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about exact tree node for source-side data protection threat; Dd.1.1 used as best approximation for unauthorized access risk at source.

title: Video Metadata Linkability
description: Metadata associated with video uploads (e.g., timestamps, device info, IP addresses) could be used to link the parent user to their activities and potentially identify them across systems.
assumptions: Metadata is collected and transmitted with video uploads

title: Video Content Identification
description: Video content stored by the Video Management Service could contain identifiable information about the parent user or other individuals, enabling identification without consent.
assumptions: Video content may contain faces, voices, or other personally identifiable information

title: Unauthorized Video Access
description: Video content stored by the Video Management Service could be accessed by unauthorized parties through security breaches, insider threats, or inadequate access controls.
assumptions: The service may have vulnerabilities or insufficient access controls

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: Video content may contain more personal data than necessary for the approval/rejection purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Full video content is processed/stored when only metadata or thumbnails might be needed

title: Identity Theft via Video Content
description: Video content could be misused for identity theft, impersonation, or deepfake creation, allowing unauthorized use of the parent user's identity.
assumptions: Video content could be extracted and misused by malicious actors

title: Child User Identifiable in Video Content
description: The Video Management Service shares video content that may contain personally identifiable information about the child user, making them identifiable to unauthorized observers.

title: Video Stream Interception During Transmission
description: The video stream in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized third parties, leading to unauthorized disclosure of the child's video content.

title: Child User May Share Video with Unauthorized Parties
description: The child user, upon receiving the video, may share or distribute it with unauthorized individuals, leading to further disclosure of the child's image and activities.

title: User Unawareness of Data Sharing with Advertisers
description: Users may not be aware that their browsing data is being shared with third-party advertisers, violating transparency expectations and consent requirements.

title: Excessive Data Sharing with Advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may share more browsing data than necessary with advertisers, violating data minimization principles and potentially exposing sensitive user information.

title: User Identification via Browsing Data in Transit
description: Browsing data transmitted between the AI Recommendation Engine and advertisers could be used to identify individual users and link their online activities across different contexts.

title: Advertiser Profiling and Secondary Use of Data
description: Third-party advertisers may use the received browsing data to create detailed user profiles beyond the intended advertising purposes, potentially violating user expectations and privacy regulations.

title: Browsing Data Interception During Transmission
description: Browsing data transmitted to advertisers could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, leading to unauthorized access to user browsing patterns and potentially sensitive information.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Government ID Images
description: The file system backend/uploads/ may be accessible to unauthorized personnel or systems, allowing them to view, download, or copy sensitive government ID images without proper authentication or authorization controls.

title: Data Integrity Compromise of Stored ID Images
description: Government ID images stored in the file system could be tampered with, altered, or corrupted by malicious actors, compromising the authenticity and reliability of the stored identification documents.

title: Unauthorized Deletion of Government ID Images
description: Stored government ID images could be deleted without proper authorization, audit trails, or retention policies, potentially violating legal requirements for data retention and preventing legitimate access to historical records.

title: Identification Through Government ID Image Sharing
description: The act of the Authentication Service sharing government ID images to the file system creates a direct identification risk, as these images contain personally identifiable information that can uniquely identify individuals.

title: Linkability of Government ID Images to Other Data
description: Government ID images shared by the Authentication Service could be linked with other datasets (e.g., transaction records, access logs) to create comprehensive profiles of individuals, potentially enabling surveillance or profiling beyond the intended purpose.

title: JWT Disclosure via localStorage XSS Vulnerability
description: Browser localStorage is accessible to JavaScript, making JWT tokens vulnerable to cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks. Malicious scripts can read and exfiltrate the stored JWT, leading to unauthorized access to user accounts and sensitive authentication data.

title: User Identifiability from JWT Contents
description: JWT tokens typically contain user identifiers (user ID, email, etc.) that can be extracted from localStorage. If the JWT is compromised, these identifiers can be used to link the token to specific individuals, enabling profiling and tracking.

title: JWT Interception During Transmission
description: If the JWT is transmitted over unencrypted HTTP or without proper TLS protection, it could be intercepted by network attackers during transit between the Authentication Service and Browser localStorage, leading to credential theft.

title: JWT Stored with Excessive Privileges
description: The Authentication Service may issue JWTs with overly broad permissions or long expiration times, increasing the risk of token misuse if the JWT is stolen from localStorage. This enables attackers to usurp user identity for extended periods.

title: Unauthorized Data Leakage from Child Profile Management Process
description: The Child Profile Management process (P3) may share child history data with the parent user (EE1) without proper authentication or authorization verification, potentially leaking sensitive child information to unauthorized parties.

title: Excessive Child Data Sharing
description: The process may share more child history data than necessary for the parent's review, violating data minimization principles and exposing unnecessary sensitive information about the child.

title: Child Identification Through Data in Transit
description: Child history data transmitted in the flow may contain identifying information that could be used to link or identify the child, even if the data is not intended for public access.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Child history data in transit may be intercepted by unauthorized third parties if the data flow is not properly encrypted or protected during transmission.

title: Parent User Data Sharing
description: The parent user (EE1) may share or disclose the child's history information to third parties after receiving it, leading to unintended data leakage beyond the intended recipient.
